text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak and U.S. Secretary of State Warren Christopher are to discuss the latest developments in the peace process during Christopher's visit to Cairo for the November 12 to 14 economic conference. The American ambassador Edward Walker said that Christopher would convey to Mubarak the United States intention to continue pushing the peace process forward.
- United States ambassador Walker says 120 U.S. companies are participating in the upcoming economic conference in Cairo.
- Mubarak receives a parliamentary delegation from Chile and is invited to visit the country.
- Egyptian Foreign Minister Amr Moussa said a proposal by British Foreign Minister Malcolm Rifkind to set up a regional body to help reduce conflicts was premature.

Rifkind, on a regional tour designed to give new impetus to the peace process, had said in the United Arab Emirates that the Middle East would benefit from a forum that includes all the countries in the region and that would "provide a framework for dialogue and collaboration."

- Prime Minister Kamal Ganzouri stresses there would be no increase in taxes and no burden on Egyptian nationals. He also reiterates that Egypt welcomes foreign, Arab and Egyptian investment and intends to rationalise spending.
- Security forces foil attempt to smuggle 50 kg of heroin.
- Insurance companies to give 1.5 million pounds to victims of the collapsed building in Heliopolis.
